subject: Hotshard degradation — private cluster throughput & p95 spike (Hightower.ai)
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@hightower.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaSOps Engineering <ops@hightower.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: private cluster p95 jump + 502s after midnight deploy

Mina / Redwood team —

We just saw a sustained p95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~1.2s on our private cluster (vpc-managed, single hotshard) starting ~01:15 PT this morning. Error rate for generate endpoints increased to ~3.4% 502/504s over a 40m window. The deploy at 00:58 was a small ops change (kernel GC params) but our rollback didn’t fully restore throughput.

Attached: support_logs_20281103.tar.gz (stripped logs), kvcache-stats-11-03.csv, screenshot of monitoring.

This is affecting our production customers (order matching). We need a short remediation plan, timeline, and confirmation if this is a Redwood runtime regression vs configuration mismatch on our end. Our CTO (Kira) is on standby for an exec call.

Can you confirm next steps?

—Jake
Jake Turner
Director, Platform Reliability
Hightower.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@hightower.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: private cluster p95 jump + 502s after midnight deploy

Jake — thanks for the signal and the artifacts. I’ve started a triage with Laura (runtime) and Evelyn (on-call infra). Immediate notes:

- We see the same p95 shift in our short-term metrics replica and the 502 pattern aligns with request queueing at the hotshard (KV cache misses spiked by ~7x).
- Rolling back the deploy partially reduced error rate but did not restore baseline p95, which suggests degraded cache/memory residency rather than the GC tunable alone.

Immediate plan (first 60 minutes):
1) Increase hotshard read-capacity by 20% (manual burst) to lift throughput while we diagnose.
2) Snapshot and preserve current KV cache state for offline analysis.
3) Run a targeted cache warm-up with production-like prefixes to rebuild residency.
4) If warm-up doesn’t restore baseline within 45m, we’ll revert to the pre-00:58 image and roll back kernel tunables entirely.

We’ll keep you updated in this thread and open a Jira (INF-9342) with live links. I’m available for a quick exec touch if Kira wants a 15-min sync.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Jake Turner <jake.turner@hightower.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: private cluster p95 jump + 502s after midnight deploy

Thanks — quick update from runtime side after initial probe: 

- Root cause hypothesis: hotshard K/V cache eviction pattern changed after GC tunable tweak combined with slightly shifted request prefix distribution. A small but high-QPS prefix expanded, causing cold misses while large keys evicted.
- Evidence: kvcache-stats shows 6.8x miss-rate increase at 01:18 and sustained >2x until warm-up. CPU and GPU utilization are normal; queue length on the hotshard jumped and hit the internal backpressure threshold which led to 502s.

Proposed mitigations (ordered):
A) Immediate: manual kvcache warm-up script (run now) that primes top 250 prefixes from the 24hr hotlist. This should recover p95 within 20–30m.
B) Near-term config: temporarily increase per-shard in-memory cap and reduce aggressive LRU eviction to preserve residency (we will limit this to 4 hours).
C) Postmort: add a guarded auto-warm path on shard restart and add a prefix-aware eviction policy.

I’ll kick off the warm-up and post logs here. If we don’t see recovery in 30m, we’ll plan the full revert (rollback image + runtime GC defaults).

Laura Bennett
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@hightower.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kira Patel <kira.patel@hightower.ai>, SaaSOps Engineering <ops@hightower.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: private cluster p95 jump + 502s after midnight deploy

Appreciate the rapid response, Mina/Laura. The warm-up started and we’re seeing p95 trend down but still ~600–700ms. We have an executive ask: if recovery stalls, Kira is requesting authorization for a partial failover to a cold standby region (costly) within 2 hours. We need a short run-rate and estimated customer impact (which endpoints, % of traffic affected) for execs — they want to understand whether credits or an ARR-level remediation will be required.

Can Redwood provide a 1-pager that summarizes root cause, immediate mitigation, estimated time-to-baseline, and recommended remediation (incl. fallback costs)? Kira is available for a 10-min call at 10:30 PT.

—Jake

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 04 Nov 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Hotshard degradation — exec summary & next steps (Hightower.ai)

Jake / Kira —

Thanks again for patience. Quick executive summary attached (drive link below) and next steps we executed: 

- Root cause (summary): interaction of a GC tunable change with an expanded high-QPS prefix led to rapid KV cache eviction on the hotshard; queueing triggered backpressure and 502/504s.
- Impact: estimated 12% of generate traffic experienced elevated p95 and ~3.4% 5xx over a 40m window; downstream order-matching queries for peak customers impacted intermittently. HubSpot deal: deal_83421.
- Immediate remediation performed: manual kvcache warm-up, temporary +20% shard capacity burst, guarded eviction relaxed (4h), monitoring thresholds adjusted. These actions reduced p95 to ~260–320ms and 5xx to ~0.3% by 14:10 PT on Nov 3.
- Further recommended work: prefix-aware eviction policy, auto-warm on restart, and a small runtime patch to prevent next-GC param regressions. Estimated engineering effort: 2–3 sprints across runtime and infra; one short-term config toggle to be ready for the next 48hrs.
- Failover cost estimate (cold region): ~USD 18k/hr for Hightower’s baseline throughput; we recommend this only if p95 > 1s sustained beyond 2 hours.
- Requested approvals: governance sign-off to grant up to one week of targeted credits for high-impact customers if postmort indicates SLA breach; Rishi to route finance approval.

Attachments / links: exec summary PDF (Drive) — https://drive.redwood.com/teams/hightower/incident-20281103/exec-summary.pdf; Jira INF-9342 — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9342

I’m scheduling a 30-min technical + commercial sync for Mon 11/06 09:00 PT to align on patch timeline and credits governance. If you need an earlier exec-only touch, Rishi and I are available.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
